title: One-to-many joins: predicting and counting rows

items.stem: A customers table has 5 customers. An orders table has 7 orders: customer A has 4 orders, customer B has 1, customer E has 2, and customers C and D have none. How many rows does customers LEFT JOIN orders (matching on customer_id) return?
Same tables as the previous question. You run customers INNER JOIN orders on customer_id and then compute COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_id), where c is the customers table. What number does it return?
Same tables again, using the LEFT JOIN from customers to orders (alias o for orders, c for customers). Which expression returns the number of orders, which is 7?

options.text: COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_id) over the joined rows

items.stem: Same tables again. Every one of the 5 customers has a credit_limit of 100 in the customers table. After the LEFT JOIN from customers to orders, what does SUM(c.credit_limit) return?

Fill in the blank with one SQL keyword so the query returns the number of customers who have placed at least one order, not the number of joined rows: SELECT COUNT(____ c.customer_id) FROM customers c INNER JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id;
